whatItDoes: Estimates the monthly payment, total cost, and total interest for repaying a student loan on a standard repayment schedule.
whyItExists: Student loans affect budgets for years, and the interplay of balance, rate, and term can add tens of thousands in interest. An estimate makes the real cost of repayment visible before you commit to a plan.
whoShouldUse: Graduates planning repayment, borrowers comparing terms, and anyone weighing extra payments against standard amortization.
useCases: Estimate monthly payments for a total loan balance
Compare repayment term lengths and their interest cost
See how extra monthly payments shorten the term
instructions: Enter your total outstanding loan balance
Enter a weighted average interest rate as a percent
Choose a repayment term in years
Read the monthly payment, total paid, and total interest
examples: $30,000 at 5.05% for 10 years -> payment approx $318, interest approx $8,140
$50,000 at 6% for 10 years -> payment approx $555, interest approx $16,610
bestPractices: Use your weighted average rate when consolidating federal and private loans
Compare the total-interest cost of a 10-year vs. 20-year term
Check income-driven options separately — they differ from standard repayment
Pay extra toward the highest-rate loan first
commonMistakes: Using an average of rates instead of a weighted average
Assuming forgiveness programs apply to every loan type
Forgetting to re-run the math after refinancing
faq: Does this include income-driven repayment? — No, it models standard amortization only.
What rate should I use? — The weighted average across all your loans is a good estimate.
Are forgiveness programs included? — No, they change payments and totals significantly.
Is my data shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
